chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, he said: Hasan ibn Ali al-Sukri narrated to us, he said: Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibn Zakariya al-Basri narrated to us, he said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn 'Umara narrated to us, from his father, from Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon them both)

He said: I asked him about the meaning of 'There is no force nor strength except by Allah'. So he said: It means: There is no force for us to turn away from disobedience to Allah except by the assistance of Allah, and there is no strength for us to perform obedience to Allah except by the success of Allah, Glorious and Exalted is He.

key_terms.حَوْل: Force or ability to turn away (from sin)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah' according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) elucidates the theological nuance of 'La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah' by distinguishing between *hawla* (the ability to turn away from sin) and *quwwah* (the strength to perform obedience). This explanation underscores the Shia doctrine of *fayd* (divine effusion), affirming that human agency is sustained entirely by God's continuous assistance (*ayn*) and empowerment (*tawfiq*), thereby balancing free will with divine grace. Such interpretation is foundational in Shia *kalam* for understanding the interplay between human effort and divine decree in spiritual development.
